html:
With two games left, the AL West remains deadlocked between Houston and Texas, and the AL Central tightened as Chicago White Sox trail Cleveland by one after both won. In the NL, Arizona's rout of San Diego kept them alive at 1.0 back of Philadelphia for the final wild card spot, though their elimination number is down to 2.

  • Eury Pérez [9 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 3.91 ERA, PAR 36] tossed a complete game shutout as Miami blanked Atlanta 3-0. (MIA)
  • Cleveland outlasted Kansas City 12-9 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing, keeping the Guardians atop the AL Central. (GUARDIANS)
  • Toronto stormed back from a 9% win probability to stun Cincinnati 6-5.
  • Boston swept a doubleheader from the Cubs, winning 4-3 and 2-0 at Fenway; Baltimore and the Yankees split their twin bill, with Pete Alonso [3-5, 2 HR | RC 114] homering twice in the Orioles' 10-2 Game 1 rout. (BAL)
  • Arizona pounded San Diego 11-4 to stay alive in the NL wild card chase, 1.0 back of Philadelphia with two to play.
  • Tarik Skubal [7 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 2.73 ERA, PAR 59] struck out 10 over seven scoreless innings as the Dodgers blanked the Giants 2-0. (LAD)
  • Munetaka Murakami [3-4, 2 HR | RC 75] hit two homers in the White Sox's 6-1 win over Colorado, keeping Chicago within a game of Cleveland. (CWS)
  • Elsewhere: Tampa Bay 2, Philadelphia 0; Washington 7, Mets 6; Detroit 8, Pittsburgh 7; Milwaukee 8, St. Louis 4; Minnesota 10, Texas 2; Athletics 6, Houston 5; Angels 7, Seattle 5. (METS) (ATHLETICS) (ANGELS)

The AL West remains deadlocked entering the final weekend, as both the Astros and Rangers won to stay tied at 79-80. Houston's victory was powered by Lucas Spence [3-4, 3 HR | RC 5]'s three-homer explosion, while Texas quietly kept pace by handling the Mets.

  • Lucas Spence hit 3 home runs to lead the Astros past the Athletics, keeping Houston tied atop the AL West. (HOU)
  • The Rangers beat the Mets behind Josh Jung [3-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 67]'s perfect day to remain tied with Houston. (TEX)
  • The Guardians edged the Red Sox 1-0 to hold a 1.0-game lead in the AL Central; the White Sox stayed within striking distance by routing the Royals, with David Sandlin [6 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 5.61 ERA, PAR 4] and Kyle Teel [2-2, 3 BB, 1 HR | RC 13] starring. (CWS)
  • The Phillies fell to the Brewers but continue to hold the final NL wild card spot. (BREWERS)
  • The Diamondbacks outslugged the Rockies 12-8 but remain 2.0 games back in the NL wild card race with only 3 to play. (DIAMONDBACKS)
  • The Yankees roared back from a 9% win probability to beat the Rays 6-4 in the day's most dramatic comeback. (RAYS)
  • The Reds edged the Braves 7-6 in the largest WPA swing of the day; the Cubs, Pirates, and Padres also picked up narrow wins. (PIRATES) (CUBS) (REDS) (PADRES)

The AL East and AL West races tightened dramatically, as Baltimore swept a doubleheader from Toronto to gain 1.5 games on the Rays, while Seattle rallied from a 16% win probability to beat Houston 6-5, pulling within 4 games in the AL West as both co-leaders Houston and Texas lost. In the NL West, both the Padres and Diamondbacks gained a game on the Dodgers, who fell 5-1 to San Diego.

  • Seattle Mariners staged the day's biggest comeback, beating Houston 6-5 after falling to 16% win probability, gaining a game in the AL West. (SEATTLE MARINERS)
  • Baltimore Orioles swept a doubleheader from Toronto, winning both games 4-2 and gaining 1.5 games in the AL wild card race. (BALTIMORE ORIOLES)
  • San Diego Padres beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-1, closing the NL West gap. (SAN DIEGO PADRES)
  • New York Yankees routed Tampa Bay 9-2 behind Ben Rice [3-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 109], who homered twice and reached 41 on the season to tie for the AL lead. (NYY)
  • Boston edged Cleveland 1-0 as Sonny Gray [6 IP, 0 ER, 3 K | 2.72 ERA, PAR 55] tossed six shutout innings, cutting into the Guardians' AL Central lead. (BOS)
  • Kansas City beat Chicago 5-4 with Maikel Garcia [3-3, 1 BB | RC 37] going 3-for-3; Cleveland's Central lead over the White Sox held at 1 game. (KC)
  • Milwaukee beat Philadelphia 4-1, and Atlanta edged Cincinnati 3-2 as Chris Sale [5.2 IP, 1 ER, 10 K | 2.16 ERA, PAR 68] struck out 10 over 5.2 innings. (ATL)
  • Washington beat Detroit 4-2, St. Louis topped Pittsburgh 5-1, the Mets beat Texas 7-2 behind a Juan Soto [1-2, 3 BB, 1 HR | RC 80] homer (NYM)

The National League contenders chipped away at both division leaders, with Washington, New York, Philadelphia, and Miami all winning to gain a game on Atlanta, while Cincinnati and Pittsburgh cut into Milwaukee's lead. The Athletics authored the day's most dramatic finish, rallying from a 2% win probability to beat the Angels 9-7.

  • The Athletics stunned the Angels 9-7 after falling to a 2% win probability. (ANGELS)
  • The Rays and Yankees split a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium, with New York taking the opener 2-0 behind Carlos Rodón [8 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 2.68 ERA, PAR 27] before Tampa Bay answered 6-1. (NYY)
  • Cleveland edged Boston 3-2 at Fenway in the day's second-most dramatic game, dropping the Red Sox a full game in the AL wild card race. (SOX)
  • Miami routed the Cubs 8-2 in the day's biggest WPA swing, with Kyle Stowers [2-4, 2 BB, 1 HR | RC 67] homering. (MIA)
  • Jared Jones [7 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 3.89 ERA, PAR 26] shut out the Cardinals over seven innings as Pittsburgh won 2-0. (PIT)
  • CJ Abrams [2-4, 2 HR | RC 95] hit two homers in Washington's 3-1 win over Detroit; Randal Grichuk [4-5, 1 HR | RC 46] and Chase Meidroth [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 79] each homered in the White Sox' 14-11 slugfest at Kansas City. (WSH) (CWS)
  • The Dodgers blanked the Padres 7-0, and Houston shut out Seattle 7-0 on the road. (PADRES)
  • Blue Jays at Orioles was postponed.

The Orioles pulled off the day's most dramatic result, rallying from a 20% win probability to beat the Blue Jays 4-3 in a game that produced a 3.03 WPA swing. The win nudged Baltimore forward in the AL wild card race while Toronto slipped a half game.

  • Pete Alonso [2-4, 2 HR | RC 108] and Gunnar Henderson [3-4, 1 HR | RC 78] powered Baltimore's comeback win over Toronto, each homering in the 4-3 result. (BAL)
  • Detroit routed Washington 9-2 behind strong outings from Keider Montero [4 IP, 0 ER, 5 K | 3.48 ERA, PAR 39] and River Ryan [3 IP, 0 ER, 3 K | 0.00 ERA, PAR 2], with Javier Báez [1-2, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 18] adding a home run; the Tigers gained a half game on AL Central-leading Cleveland. (DET)
  • San Francisco beat Minnesota 5-2 as Drew Gilbert [3-4, 1 HR | RC 43] homered and Blade Tidwell [3.1 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 4.48 ERA, PAR 9] turned in the Giants' top pitching line; SF gained a half game on the NL West-leading Dodgers. (SF)
  • Shane Baz [6.2 IP, 3 ER, 2 K | 4.12 ERA, PAR 42] went 6.2 innings for Baltimore in the Orioles' one-run win. (BAL)
  • Yohandy Morales [1-1, 1 HR | RC 7] hit a home run in Washington's loss. (WSH)

The AL West race tightened as the Rangers fell to the Blue Jays and the Mariners won, cutting into Texas's slim division lead. Seattle picked up a full game and Houston gained a half-game despite losing, leaving the Rangers just one up on the Astros.

  • Kade Anderson [7 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 4.21 ERA, PAR 7] and the Mariners edged the Rockies 2-1 at Coors Field to gain ground in the AL West. (SEA)
  • Hunter Brown [5 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 3.26 ERA, PAR 28] dominated as the Braves beat the Astros 4-2, though Houston still gained on Texas in the division. (HOU)
  • Gavin Williams [7 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 3.63 ERA, PAR 50] tossed seven shutout innings as the Guardians blanked the Athletics 1-0 in one of the day's tightest games. (CLE)
  • The Diamondbacks stormed back from a 16% win probability to beat the Yankees 8-4, gaining half a game in the NL wild card while New York lost ground in the AL East. (YANKEES)
  • The Pirates outlasted the Royals 4-3 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing. (ROYALS)
  • Jake Cronenworth [3-4, 2 HR | RC 36] homered twice as the Padres beat the Marlins 7-3. (SD)
  • Iván Herrera [2-4, 2 HR | RC 81] also went deep twice in the Cardinals' 5-3 win over the Nationals. (STL)
  • Dean Kremer [6 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 4.98 ERA, PAR 10] shut out the Angels over six innings as the Twins rolled 8-0. (MIN)

The Angels pulled off the day's most dramatic finish, rallying from a 5% win probability to beat the Twins 6-5 in the game with the largest WPA swing on the board. In the wild card picture, the Mets, Nationals, Diamondbacks, Pirates, and Rockies all gained ground, while the Phillies' loss pushed them further behind Atlanta in the NL East.

  • Los Angeles Angels stunned the Minnesota Twins 6-5 after falling to a 5% win probability. (MINNESOTA TWINS)
  • Brayan Bello [8 IP, 1 ER, 11 K | 4.50 ERA, PAR 22] led all pitchers on the day, but the Red Sox still fell 2-1 to the Rays, dropping Boston further back in the AL East. (BOS)
  • Angel Martínez [4-5, 2 HR | RC 50] powered Cleveland's 12-6 rout of the Athletics with a two-homer game. (CLE)
  • New York Mets routed the Phillies 10-3 behind Carson Benge [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 81], gaining a game in the NL wild card race. (NYM)
  • Washington beat St. Louis 8-5 in a game with the day's second-largest WPA swing, with Andrew Alvarez [6 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 3.17 ERA, PAR 34] dominating on the mound. (WSH)
  • Milwaukee edged Baltimore 1-0 as Robert Gasser [7 IP, 0 ER, 2 K | 4.02 ERA, PAR 21] tossed seven scoreless. (MIL)
  • Arizona (over Yankees), Pittsburgh (over Royals), and Colorado (over Mariners) all won to gain ground in the NL wild card chase. (ROYALS) (MARINERS) (YANKEES)
  • Dodgers pounded the Giants 10-4 with Mookie Betts [4-4, 1 BB | RC 68] going 4-for-4. (LAD)

The AL East race tightened as both the Red Sox and Yankees picked up a game on the idle-losing Rays, with Boston beating Tampa Bay directly and New York routing Arizona. Meanwhile, the Brewers survived a wild one in Baltimore in the day's most dramatic finish, a 5.08 WPA swing.

  • Brewers edged the Orioles 6-5 in the day's most dramatic game. (BREWERS)
  • Red Sox 4, Rays 2: Boston pulled within 9.5 games of first in the AL East. (SOX) (RAYS)
  • Yankees 9, Diamondbacks 2: Ben Rice [2-3, 2 BB, 1 HR | RC 106] homered as New York closed to 4.0 GB in the AL East. (NYY)
  • Tigers stormed back from a 3% win probability to beat the White Sox 11-8, powered by Hao-Yu Lee [4-5, 1 HR | RC 41]. (DET)
  • Mariners 5, Rockies 4: Seattle gained ground on the Astros in the AL West. (MARINERS) (ASTROS)
  • Twins blanked the Angels 3-0 behind Connor Prielipp [7 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 4.95 ERA, PAR 22]'s dominant start. (MIN)
  • Dodgers 8, Giants 2: Mookie Betts [3-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 64] launched two homers; Tyler Glasnow [6 IP, 2 ER, 10 K | 3.48 ERA, PAR 21] struck out 10. (LAD)
  • Other results: Reds over Cubs 6-4, Pirates over Royals 8-5, Guardians over A's 5-3, Mets over Phillies 6-3, Rangers over Blue Jays 7-1, Braves over Astros 6-2, Nationals over Cardinals 9-1, Padres over Marlins 8-2. (CUBS) (ROYALS) (GUARDIANS) (PHILLIES) (JAYS) (BRAVES) (NATIONALS) (MARLINS)

The Pirates' 7-4 win over Milwaukee cut into the Brewers' NL Central lead, with Chicago and St. Louis also gaining a half-game on the division leader. Meanwhile, Boston pulled off the day's most improbable rally, climbing back from a 9% win probability to beat Texas 4-3 and deal the Rangers a costly loss in the AL wild card race.

  • Henry Davis [1-2, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 20] and the Pirates knocked off Milwaukee 7-4, gaining a full game in the NL Central. (PIT)
  • Boston stunned Texas 4-3 after falling to 9% win probability, dropping the Rangers a game in the AL wild card chase. (RANGERS)
  • Walbert Ureña [7 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 2.75 ERA, PAR 46] dominated as the Angels edged Minnesota 5-4 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing. (LAA)
  • Kyle Tucker [4-5, 1 HR | RC 65] powered the Dodgers past Cincinnati 8-2, pushing the Reds back in the NL wild card race. (LAD)
  • Aaron Nola [7 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 4.50 ERA, PAR 25] tossed seven shutout innings as Philadelphia blanked the Mets 3-0, gaining a half-game on Atlanta in the NL East. (PHI)
  • Xander Bogaerts [3-5, 1 HR | RC 55] and Ty France [3-4, 1 BB | RC 76] led San Diego to a 9-2 rout of Colorado at Coors Field. (SD)
  • Ethan Pecko [5.2 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 3.83 ERA, PAR 4] and Houston beat Kansas City 6-2 to hold the AL West lead over Texas. (HOU)
  • Tampa Bay routed the Athletics 10-1, and the White Sox edged Detroit 3-1 to stay tied atop the AL Central. (ATHLETICS) (SOX)

The NL West race tightened dramatically as both the Padres and Giants gained a full game on the idle-losing Dodgers, who fell in Cincinnati. San Diego's rout in Colorado and San Francisco's one-run win in St. Louis pulled the Padres to within 9.0 GB, while the Reds handed Los Angeles a rare stumble.

  • Pete Crow-Armstrong [3-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 129] homered twice as the Cubs routed the Braves 8-4, with Alex Bregman [3-4, 1 HR | RC 96] also going deep. (CHC)
  • The Twins edged the Yankees 5-4 in the day's most dramatic game (5.77 WPA swing), behind six scoreless from Zebby Matthews [6 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 4.75 ERA, PAR 17]; New York lost a game in the AL East. (MIN)
  • Zack Wheeler [7 IP, 0 ER, 5 K | 3.00 ERA, PAR 46] tossed seven shutout innings as the Phillies blanked the Nationals 3-0, gaining a game in the NL East. (PHI)
  • The Giants beat the Cardinals 6-5 behind Anthony Molina [5.2 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 4.18 ERA, PAR 7], gaining ground in the NL West. (SF)
  • The Padres crushed the Rockies 9-3 as Ethan Salas [2-4, 2 HR | RC 2] homered twice. (SD)
  • The Brewers rallied from a 28% win probability to beat the Pirates 5-4. (BREWERS)
  • The Mariners cruised past the Angels 7-2, gaining a full game in the AL West on Houston. (MARINERS)
  • The Rays, Blue Jays, Guardians, Royals, Orioles, Rangers, and Marlins also picked up wins. (GUARDIANS) (JAYS) (RAYS) (ORIOLES) (RANGERS) (ROYALS) (MARLINS)

The AL Central race tightened dramatically as both the Guardians and Tigers gained ground on the first-place White Sox, with Cleveland now just a half-game back after edging Chicago in a 4.07 WPA swing. Meanwhile, the Orioles authored the day's most stunning comeback, rallying from a 9% win probability to stun the Mets 7-5.

  • Baltimore rallied from a 9% win probability to defeat the Mets 7-5, the day's biggest comeback. (METS)
  • Cleveland edged the White Sox 7-6 to close within a half-game of the AL Central lead, while Detroit routed Toronto 10-1 to gain further ground. (SOX)
  • Yoshinobu Yamamoto [7 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 2.51 ERA, PAR 62] was dominant as the Dodgers blanked the Reds 4-0. (LAD)
  • Cole Carrigg [4-5, 2 HR | RC 46] homered twice as the Rockies hammered the Padres 9-3. (COL)
  • Jeremy Peña [3-4, 2 HR | RC 60] launched two homers to lift the Astros past the Royals 4-2. (HOU)
  • Max Fried [7 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 2.63 ERA, PAR 40] and Cody Bellinger [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 71] powered the Yankees to an 8-1 win over the Twins. (NYY)
  • Other results: Rays 2, Athletics 1; Brewers 5, Pirates 1; Nationals 6, Phillies 3; Braves 6, Cubs 3; Giants 10, Cardinals 3; Rangers 4, Red Sox 2; Angels 2, Mariners 1; Marlins 4, Diamondbacks 2. (ATHLETICS) (SOX) (BREWERS) (PHILLIES) (BRAVES) (GIANTS) (MARINERS) (MARLINS)

The Detroit Tigers pulled off the day's most dramatic finish, edging Toronto 6-5 in a game that produced the largest WPA swing of the day and gained Detroit a full game in the AL wild card race. Meanwhile, division leaders took hits across the board, with the Rays, Astros, Braves, and Brewers all losing ground.

  • Tarik Skubal [7 IP, 0 ER, 9 K | 2.71 ERA, PAR 55] and the Dodgers beat the Reds 4-1, with Cincinnati falling further back in the NL Central. (LAD)
  • The White Sox topped the Guardians 7-3, dropping Cleveland a full game in the AL Central race. (SOX)
  • The Tigers edged the Blue Jays 6-5 in the day's most dramatic game, gaining a game in the AL wild card chase. (TIGERS)
  • The Orioles beat the Mets 2-1 behind Jonah Tong [6 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 3.43 ERA, PAR 5]'s strong outing in a losing effort, gaining ground in the AL East while New York lost a game in the NL wild card race. (NYM)
  • Pete Crow-Armstrong [4-5, 1 HR | RC 125] homered and went 4-for-5 as the Cubs beat the Braves 7-3, closing ground in the NL Central. (CHC)
  • Will Warren [5.2 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 3.89 ERA, PAR 33] and the Yankees routed the Twins 8-3, cutting into the Rays' AL East lead. (NYY)
  • The Diamondbacks stunned the Marlins 8-7, rallying from a 5% win probability; Lars Nootbaar [3-5, 1 HR | RC 34] homered while Jakob Marsee [3-4, 1 HR | RC 58] homered for Miami. (AZ)
  • The Padres outslugged the Rockies 8-7, and the Cardinals beat the Giants 2-1 behind Quinn Mathews [6.2 IP, 1 ER, 8 K | 3.64 ERA, PAR 10]. (STL)

The Athletics pulled off the day's most stunning result, storming back from a 6% win probability to beat the Mariners 8-7 in the game with the largest WPA swing of the day. The comeback loss cost Seattle ground in the AL West, though the Mariners still gained on Houston, who also lost as Texas moved to within a game of the division lead.

  • Lawrence Butler [2-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 53] and the Athletics rallied past Seattle 8-7 after falling to a 6% win probability, the day's biggest comeback. (ATH)
  • Texas beat Arizona 7-6 to pull within 1.0 GB of Houston in the AL West, while the Diamondbacks lost ground in the NL wild card chase. (DIAMONDBACKS)
  • San Diego routed San Francisco 6-4 to close within 9.0 GB of the Dodgers, who fell 6-4 to Miami as the Marlins gained on Atlanta in the NL East. (DODGERS)
  • Washington edged the Angels 6-5, also gaining a game on the Braves, who dropped a 9-4 decision to Philadelphia at Truist Park. (ANGELS) (BRAVES)
  • Cam Schlittler [6 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 1.95 ERA, PAR 77] tossed six shutout innings as the Yankees blanked the Mets 2-0 in the Subway Series matchup. (NYY)
  • Payton Tolle [6 IP, 0 ER, 7 K | 3.02 ERA, PAR 47] delivered six scoreless frames in Boston's 4-1 win over Kansas City; Toronto pounded Baltimore 8-1 behind a 4-for-5 day from Vladimir Guerrero Jr. [4-5, 1 HR | RC 62] (BOS) (TOR)
  • Randy Arozarena [3-5, 2 HR | RC 94] homered twice for Seattle in the loss, while Jonathan Aranda [2-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 86] also went deep twice in Tampa Bay's 14-4 rout of Houston. (SEA) (TB)
  • Detroit beat Colorado 8-1 behind Jackson Jobe [6.1 IP, 1 ER, 8 K | 3.95 ERA, PAR 6], Cleveland routed Minnesota 9-2, Cincinnati ed (DET)

The Braves pulled off the day's most consequential result, rallying from a 12% win probability to beat the Phillies 6-5 and push their NL East lead to 5.0 games. In the AL Central, all three chasers gained on the White Sox, tightening the division to a half-game race between Chicago and Cleveland.

  • Ronald Acuña Jr. [1-5 | RC 54] and the Braves stunned the Phillies 6-5 in the day's biggest comeback, trimming Philadelphia's deficit hopes in the NL East. (ATL)
  • The Brewers demolished the Reds 20-0, powered by an 8-run 5th inning, with Dustin May [6 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 4.50 ERA, PAR 31] tossing 6 shutout innings and Brice Turang [3-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 83] leading all hitters. (MIL)
  • The Guardians, Tigers and Royals all won, each gaining a game on the AL Central-leading White Sox, who lost 7-3 to the Cardinals. (TIGERS) (ROYALS) (SOX) (GUARDIANS)
  • The Athletics edged the Mariners 6-5, gaining ground in the AL West while Seattle slipped in the wild card chase. (MARINERS)
  • Carlos Rodón [6.1 IP, 1 ER, 8 K | 2.95 ERA, PAR 21] and the Yankees beat the Mets 6-4 in the Subway Series, with Ben Rice [3-4, 1 HR | RC 98] homering. (NYY)
  • The Rays kept pace atop the AL East as Drew Rasmussen [7 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 2.81 ERA, PAR 56] dominated the Astros over 7 innings in a 3-1 win. (TB)
  • The Dodgers rolled past the Marlins 6-2 behind a big day from Kyle Tucker [3-3, 1 HR | RC 60]. (LAD)
  • The Diamondbacks routed the Rangers 9-1, and the Padres beat the Giants 7-5 to stay in the NL wild card mix. (RANGERS) (PADRES)
